strings.name: Larry Page
strings.summary: Page and Sergey Brin researched web-link analysis at Stanford and went on to found Google. Technologies such as PageRank helped improve online information retrieval, while the company later expanded into video, mobile operating systems and cloud services. Page twice took part in Google’s day-to-day management and helped create the Alphabet structure, stepping down as the group’s CEO in 2019.
strings.coverageNote: Selected public biographical and corporate-management milestones from 1973 to 2019. Later investments and private activities are not continuously tracked.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Bachelor of engineering, University of Michigan; graduate studies in computer science, Stanford University
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Associated organizations
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: PageRank link analysis
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Researched methods with Brin for assessing importance through links between webpages, forming the technical basis of early Google search.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Co-founding Google
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Turned a research project into a search company that changed how people find information online.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: Creating the Alphabet structure
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: Became Alphabet’s CEO in 2015, with Google and other businesses operating separately under the group.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Steps down as Alphabet CEO
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Together with Brin, announced a management change under which Sundar Pichai became CEO of both Google and Alphabet.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Becomes Alphabet CEO
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Google was reorganized under Alphabet; Page took charge of the new group while Pichai became Google’s CEO.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Returns to Google’s day-to-day operations
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Succeeded Eric Schmidt as CEO, also taking responsibility for product and technology strategy.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Google acquires YouTube
strings.timeline.event-04.text: During his participation in the company’s leadership, Google acquired YouTube and expanded its video services.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Google goes public
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Google entered public capital markets, obtaining broader financial support for the expansion of its search business.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Management responsibilities change
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Eric Schmidt became CEO; Page moved to a product leadership role while remaining involved in running the company.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Co-founds Google
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Commercialized their search research with Brin, secured early investment and established an office in a California garage.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Begins graduate work at Stanford
strings.timeline.event-08.text: After completing his undergraduate degree at Michigan, went to Stanford, met Brin and gradually began collaborating on search.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Michigan
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in the Lansing area; later studied engineering at the University of Michigan and continued his education at Stanford.
